messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: auth-service high error rate detected from multiple discrete IP clusters in LATAM — 5xxs and elevated failed login rate. See alert: https://alerts.internal/redwood/2793456789

maria_sre: I'm on it. spike started ~ 22:04 UTC, failure rate ~12%. Login attempts are ~35k/min, 90% come from ~2000 IPs. Looks like credential stuffing + proxy farm.

alex_oncall: Confirmed. Sessions per IP ~17, many distinct user-agents that look automated. Impact: login latency up, some customers reporting 429s from throttles.

jordan_eng: Any correlated embedding or generation spikes?

maria_sre: Embeddings traffic elevated for a handful of API keys (prob abused). Generation endpoints normal. Primary user impact: auth failures and temporary sign-in slowdowns.

viv_support: We already have 3 support tickets complaining about slow logins and app errors. Tier-1 triage: notify top-10 affected customers.

alex_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan proposal: 1) push temporary WAF IP block list for identified CIDR clusters, 2) enable per-key short cooldown on auth endpoints (20s), 3) reduce embedding batch window for API keys with anomalous rate, 4) prepare customer notice if we need to throttle further. Thoughts?

jordan_eng: +1 on WAF and per-key cooldown. For embeddings, recommend disabling bulk/batch endpoints for suspect keys to avoid collateral. We can hotpatch the gateway with a small rule: if key in suspect_set -> reject batch requests with 403 + guidance.

edge_waf_bot: New WAF rule candidate generated: BLOCK for 5 anonymous ASN ranges and 12 CIDRs. Rule id draft: waf-cs-2793. Preview traffic match: ~0.6% of total traffic but 78% of auth probes.

maria_sre: Deploying WAF rule in monitor mode for 2 minutes to verify. Will escalate to block if match looks correct.

alex_oncall: rolling out per-key cooldown now: adding token-bucket limiter per api_key on /v1/auth/login with burst=5, rate=3req/min for flagged keys.

jordan_eng: Pushing gateway change to disable embeddings/batch for flagged keys. Snippet: ```if is_flagged(key): return 403, {"error":"batch disabled for suspected abuse"}```

viv_support: Drafting customer note: short heads-up about transient login throttles due to automated abuse; we'll share affected customers list once SRE confirms.

maria_sre: WAF monitor results: matches look precise. Moving to block. Applying waf-cs-2793 -> BLOCK now.

edge_waf_bot: waf-cs-2793: rollout complete. Blocked ~3.1M requests in last 60s from rule, error rate on auth dropped from 12% -> 3% in 90s.

alex_oncall: Good signal. Starting to unflag benign false positives after quick sample review. So far 2 developer IP ranges were flagged, removed.

jordan_eng: We still see anomalous rates from a set of API keys. Running quick rate regression on those keys to determine if compromised. Can we force rotate API keys for the top 5 suspicious keys and notify owners?

maria_sre: Initiating forced key rotation for 5 keys (IDs redacted). Sending owner emails via support.

viv_support: Sent notification templates and short troubleshooting steps. Marked tickets with rollback instructions.

alex_oncall: Monitoring metrics: auth latency back to baseline, failed login attempts reduced 85%. Embedding request failures up ~1% due to batch disables for flagged keys (expected).

sam_product: Any customer-visible outage or SLO breaches? We should prepare a brief post-incident note if customers were rate-limited unexpectedly.

maria_sre: No measurable SLO breach for hosted API overall. A handful of affected customers saw 403s/429s. Recommend customer note targeted to affected accounts only.

jordan_eng: Action items: 1) keep WAF blocks for 2 hours then reevaluate, 2) keep per-key cooldown for 24h, 3) complete key rotations and confirm owners reauth, 4) re-enable batch endpoints for keys cleared by manual review. I'll open a short runbook entry for this attack pattern.

viv_support: I'll follow up with each affected customer and include mitigation timeline.

alex_oncall: Oncall handing off to maria for long-tail monitoring. maria — please escalate if we see re-escalation or new vectors (embed endpoints shifting origin).

maria_sre: Taking handoff. I'll monitor for 6 hours and post updates. Closing paging notification unless something jumps. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident page created: https://incidents.internal/2793456789 — summary: credential-stuffing via proxy farm, WAF blocks + per-key throttles applied, limited customer impact.

viv_support: Copy. Preparing targeted customer advisories now.

maria_sre: Update 22:25 UTC: no new surges. WAF blocks remain in place. I'll start phased relaxation at 23:00 UTC if stable.

alex_oncall: Thanks all. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
